title: edgecase-unit-econ-jotter
content:
Purpose: quick napkin math + hypotheses for hybrid pricing experiment that blends concurrency, warm-cache credits, and per-token alignment. Not a policy doc — just thinking out loud.

High-level idea: charge a small per-active-session base (to amortize model load + cold-starts + KV warm-up) + per-token usage with dynamic multiplier when requests are latency-sensitive (SLO premium). Introduce a tiny burst buffer of credits that decays per-minute to allow short bursts without overcharging.

Key assumptions (plausible placeholders):
- GPU cost: $6.50 / GPU-hour (p50 reserved amortized)
- Effective serving throughput for target model (quantized 4bit): 1800 tokens / GPU-minute ~= 30 tokens/sec under sustained batching with tail latency targets
- Average tokens per interactive session: 1,600 tokens (includes prompts + assistant reply history)
- Warm-cache reuse: 45% of sessions hit a prefix cache saving ~18% tokens on avg
- Expected concurrency per customer for PLG cohort: 2.4 active sessions on average during peak window

Derived numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Tokens per GPU-hour ~= 30 tokens/s * 3600s = 108k tokens / hour
- Raw GPU $/1k tokens = ($6.50 / 108000) * 1000 ~= $0.0602 per 1k tokens (infrastructure only)
- Add infra overhead + infra ops + network + model licensing buffer -> multiply by 2.2 => ~$0.133 / 1k tokens as internal break-even

Session amortization approach:
- Charge a small active-session fee to absorb cold-start/warm-up: formula: session_fee = (cold_start_cost * p_cold + avg_warm_cost) / expected_sessions_per_hour_for_customer
- Plug numbers: assume cold_start_cost = $0.04 (model load + KV miss warmup measured), p_cold for PLG traffic ~0.18, avg_warm_cost = $0.01 => expected per-session amort = (0.04*0.18+0.01)/1 ~= $0.0172 =~ 1.72 cents
- If we convert to token-equivalent at $0.133/1k => session_fee ~ 130 tokens worth

Burst buffer / decay credit model (sketch):
- Each account gets a small burst-credit bucket per hour (e.g., 400 tokens) that decays linearly over 60 minutes. First 400 tokens consumed in a rolling hour do not trigger concurrency surcharge.
- Rationale: encourages interactivity without punitive short-term spikes; still charges sustained heavy users on tokens.

Latency SLO multiplier:
- Offer two tiers of latency: standard (best-effort, cheapest) and premium (latency SLOs, reserved concurrency).
- For premium requests, add a multiplier 1.25x on per-token price or take them from reserved capacity (booked commit). This gives signal for routing + capacity planning.

Example customer walk-through (PLG app):
- Customer A: 2.4 avg concurrent sessions peak, 15k tokens/day per active user, 30% prefix reuse.
- Daily infra cost estimate per active user: tokens/day = 15k -> token cost = (15 * $0.133) = $1.995/day per user; add session fees distributed across sessions (if 6 sessions/day * $0.0172 = $0.1032) => ~$2.10/day => ~$63/mo per heavy active user (infra-only).
- Packaging implication: Starter plan could bundle 60k tokens/mo + 20 session-base-units; priced above break-even with margin. Dedicated/commit needed for SLO premium.

Edge cases and behavioral levers (things I want to test):
- Short-conversation myopia: tiny sessions (<200 tokens) blow up per-session fee. Consider a per-user daily floor (so users doing many short sessions get a daily cap).
- Prefix-heavy agents (system-message reuse) should be rewarded by discounting token price when reuse rate > 60%. Operationally detect and apply a reuse-discount flag for that customer.
- Cold-start cost spikes if model switches or history grows huge; add model-switch surcharge or a background pre-warm job option for dedicated customers.

Open questions / data to pull:
- Real measured p_cold across PLG traffic and distribution of session lengths (need histograms).
- Actual tokens / GPU-hour for our quantized runs at the bucketed sequence lengths (100/512/2048). My effective throughput numbers above are guesses.
- Cache hit behavior: rate of prefix reuse between sessions and across users in a workspace.
- Operational cost composition: what percent of infra $/hour is networking, orchestration, KMS, logging, etc. (to set correct markup).

Quick experiments to run (implementation notes):
- Simulator: run discrete-event sim for customers with simple heuristics (session arrival rate, tokens/session, prefix reuse) to compare revenue vs cost under: pure per-token, token + session fee, token + burst credits, token + SLO multiplier.
- Instrument: sample real traffic for two weeks and compute p_cold, tokens per session quantiles, 95/99 latency tails per model.
- A/B price test: small cohort opt-in to session-bundles (e.g., 300 sessions/mo + 1M tokens) vs pure token plan, measure churn/usage.

Notes on UX and billing clarity (important):
- Users hate opaque session fees; present as "active-session buffer" and show estimated token-equivalent.
- Visualize burst credits on Console and in SDK responses (x credits remaining in bucket, decay TTL).
- Provide a calculator (console widget) showing example customer economics given tokens/day and sessions/day.

Next steps (me):
- Talk to infra team for real $/GPU-hour and measured throughput by model (@Eli T)
- Draft simulator proto in GH repo (link below)
- Pull sample telemetry (product-analytics) for session histograms

Signed-off: Priya (raw thinking)
